text:
Alex: hi team — quick handoff for the ongoing eu-central-1 token auth flaps. Pager triggered ~30m ago, error spike on /v1/regen endpoints, auth failures returning 500/502 from tokenstore. Impact: some private deployment customers and a subset of hosted regen requests. Incident INC-2026-78 created. :rotating_light:

Morgan: context — started around 08:12 UTC. Tokenstore auth service (eu) shows intermittent DB connection timeouts after a config push to the pool manager. Metrics: auth-error-rate p95 jump to 4% (usual ~0.05%), regen error rate p95 up ~120ms tail + 5% failures. Customers reporting: cust-A (lossy), cust-B (failed jobs), cust-C (rate-limited backfills).

Sam: mitigation in progress — we warmed eu-dedicated-01 and started incremental traffic split (20% -> dedicated) at 08:28 UTC. Observed reduction in auth errors for routed traffic. Will continue gradual ramp if stable. :+1:

deploy-bot: deploy started by @Sam: commit 9f3a2b7 — revert of pool-manager config. CI -> canary -> staged. Logs: 
```
2026-03-15T08:26:02Z pool-manager: applying config revert
2026-03-15T08:27:30Z healthcheck: eu-tokenstore -> OK
```

pagerduty-bot: pagerduty incident INC-2026-78 acknowledged by Morgan at 08:15 UTC. Escalation policy: oncall -> sec-eng -> eng-sre.

Alex: current ownership for next shift window — Morgan is primary for the next 4h, Sam is secondary until 12:30 UTC. Jess will be backup for console escalations but is unavailable for deeper SRE-level swaps after 11:00 UTC (coverage gap). If it looks like a multi-region failover we should loop in eng-sre immediately.

Morgan: runbook pointers — follow runbook: https://wiki.redwood.company/runbooks/token-auth-failover (steps 1–4 for quick failover). Key commands below to check and (if needed) force routing: 
```
# check auth error rate
curl -s "https://monitoring/api/series?metric=auth.error_rate&region=eu-central-1" | jq .
# route 100% to dedicated pool (if automated ramp fails)
./ops/traffic-control route --region eu-central-1 --pool eu-dedicated-01 --percent 100
# quick revert of pool-manager config (last known good)
./ops/deploy revert --service pool-manager --commit 9f3a2b7
```

Sam: note on safe windows — if we hit >3% sustained auth errors for 10m, escalate to eng-sre and consider read-only fallback for embeddings/regeneration (customers get degraded experience but lower error volume). Command to enable read-only fallback: 
```
./ops/fallback enable --service regen --mode read-only --region eu-central-1
```

Alex: customer comms — CS drafted a short note for cust-A/cust-B with rollback ETA ~30–45m if revert completes. No broad outage declared yet, but we're tracking. Please copy CS on any change.

Morgan: action items for incoming shift (bullet list):
- monitor auth-error-rate dashboard (link pinned in channel) every 5m
- continue canary -> ramp if healthy, stop ramp if error rate rises >0.5% on canary
- keep pages for any customer-visible 5xx spikes
- if deploy fails, run revert command from runbook and route traffic to eu-dedicated-01 (manual)
- coordinate with eng-sre if we need cross-region failover

Sam: FYI there's a potential flappy connection pool setting that the revert addresses; postmortem item likely. I'll follow up with the pool-manager owner.

Jess: acknowledging coverage gap — I'll be available for console and CS handoffs until 11:00 UTC. After that, please ping eng-sre leads for coverage.

Alex: wrapping up — primary/secondary set (Morgan/Sam). Current mitigations: canary revert deploy in progress, 20% traffic to dedicated, read-only fallback on standby. Customer impact limited to a few customers; postmortem to follow. Hand off to @Morgan; I'll be reachable if escalation required. :white_check_mark:
